items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Ken; Ken is mentioned by the interviewer as 'Deacon Lawyer, Ken' in the context of telling stories about the old days.

ctx.x: I used to get up there. I used to get up there. I was like a monkey. I would keep my mind shut. And I was getting the money. So you all, man, go fight. Make a fool out of yourself. I was getting the money. I was getting the money. If the father would tell me, if he'd tell me that this, this pussy was black, I'd say, yeah, you were right. You were wrong. But this father wouldn't argue. I wouldn't argue with nobody. Hmm. You're right. But they wouldn't argue. They wouldn't tell the man that's standing, the man…

Deacon Lawyer, Ken, made a classical remark. He always tells you about the old days. You know that, Raymond? I mean, I'm on a job. He always tells you about the old days. I'm on a job. No, yeah, when they call a Deacon. Yeah, he was up there. And we were talking about Tom. He was saying about, in the early days, people before Tom Brown went to Chicago, you know? And somebody in the group, or maybe it was myself, said, well, according to the records, you know, Tom Brown was the first one who took a white band to…

That's not my story. No, no. Tom Brown went up and he came back. Then that's where Nick went up. Nick and Eddie Nunez. Yeah, but the Yellow Nunez went up before Nick. And Yellow. Yellow went with Nick.
